title: The Writing System That Saved My Brain (Learn Faster & Think Clearly)

sentences.en: If you don't know what skill to learn Learn to write.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道该学什么技能，那就学写作。

sentences.en: Even if you don't consider yourself a writer, or even if that thought has never crossed your brain.
sentences.zh: 哪怕你不觉得自己是写作者，哪怕这个念头从未在你脑中闪过。

sentences.en: Because writing teaches you how to think, how to learn any skill fast, and how to attract an audience that supports your work, which is absolutely needed.
sentences.zh: 因为写作教你如何思考，如何快速学会任何技能，如何吸引一群支持你工作的受众，而这绝对必不可少。

sentences.en: If you want to build your own business or just do any kind of independent, creative or meaningful work.
sentences.zh: 如果你想建立自己的一人企业，或者做任何独立的、创造性的、有意义的工作。

sentences.en: And in the age of AI thinking, learning and distribution, or getting your value in front of other people so you actually have the chance of being paid are timeless skills.
sentences.zh: 在 AI 时代，思考、学习和分发——也就是把你的价值推到别人面前，让你真正有机会获得报酬——是永远不会过时的技能。

sentences.en: Writing allows you to practice them all while building digital leverage as a byproduct.
sentences.zh: 写作让你同时练习所有这些技能，同时把数字杠杆作为副产品建立起来。

sentences.en: Now, I never thought that I would become a writer.
sentences.zh: 我从来没想过自己会成为一个写作者。

sentences.en: I still don't even call myself one, but that's what I do on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我到现在甚至都不这么称呼自己，但这就是我每天在做的事。

sentences.en: Because as a business owner or someone who wants to start and build their own thing, that's what you do.
sentences.zh: 因为作为一个企业主，或者一个想开创和建立自己事业的人，这就是你要做的事。

sentences.en: You market, you advertise, you write captions, you write posts, you write emails.
sentences.zh: 你做营销，做广告，写标题，写帖子，写邮件。

sentences.en: Literally any type of communication you do with your customers or your business partners comes down to writing.
sentences.zh: 你与客户或商业伙伴之间的任何形式的沟通，归根结底都是写作。

sentences.en: So if you actually incorporate that as a daily habit and practice to make it better, then that's a great thing, because that's what the entirety of your business hangs on.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你真的把它作为一个日常习惯和练习，让它变得更好，那是一件很棒的事，因为你的整个企业都挂在这上面。

sentences.en: And I don't even look the part.
sentences.zh: 而且我看起来根本不像。

sentences.en: I don't look like a writer.
sentences.zh: 我看起来不像一个写作者。

sentences.en: I'm just a big, dumb meat head who fell in love with deep ideas and by all measures, writing as a simple morning habit as completely altered the direction of my life and the direction outcome of my mind.
sentences.zh: 我只是一个爱上了深刻思想的大块头傻肌肉男，而无论怎么衡量，写作作为一个简单的晨间习惯，已经彻底改变了我的人生方向和我心智的产出结果。

sentences.en: Because when I was a kid, I would always look up to people who were very articulate with their thoughts, and I never thought that my brain was capable of doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 因为我小时候总是仰慕那些能非常清晰表达自己想法的人，而我从不认为我的大脑有能力做到同样的事。

sentences.en: People like Jordan Peterson, Alan Watts, etc. and I just thought that my brain didn't work that way until I started writing, and I could actually feel myself getting smarter and more articulate and beyond being able to think and learn faster.
sentences.zh: 像 Jordan Peterson、Alan Watts 这样的人，我就觉得我的大脑不是那样运作的，直到我开始写作，我真的能感觉到自己变得更聪明、更善于表达，而且不止是能更快地思考和学习了。

sentences.en: Writing is a modern form of leverage that anyone has access to.
sentences.zh: 写作是一种任何人都能接触到的现代杠杆形式。

sentences.en: That's what we're going to go over in the first section of this video, and you're going to walk away and be like, Holy shit.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在这个视频第一部分要讲的内容，你会看完后感叹，我靠。

sentences.en: I had no idea that writing something so simple that we all have access to can be so powerful.
sentences.zh: 我完全没想到，写作这么简单、我们人人都能做的事，竟然可以如此强大。

sentences.en: As many of you know, my entire business was built on 1 to 2 hours every single morning of writing.
sentences.zh: 正如你们很多人所知，我的整个事业都建立在每天早上 1 到 2 小时的写作之上。

sentences.en: Because how do you get customers in today's world writing?
sentences.zh: 因为在当今世界，你怎么获得客户？写作。

sentences.en: So in this video, I want to show you my system for capturing ideas and writing content worth reading.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个视频里，我想向你展示我捕捉想法和写出值得阅读的内容的系统。

sentences.en: But I also want to show you why this path is more viable than ever, and why it will transform how your brain interacts with reality.
sentences.zh: 但我也想向你展示，为什么这条路比以往任何时候都更可行，以及它将如何改变你的大脑与现实互动的方式。

sentences.en: And yes, it really is that deep.
sentences.zh: 没错，它真的就这么深刻。

sentences.en: So let's begin.
sentences.zh: 那我们开始吧。

sentences.en: First we're going to talk about old leverage versus new leverage.
sentences.zh: 首先我们来谈谈旧杠杆与新杠杆。

sentences.en: And this is the secret to modern success.
sentences.zh: 这就是现代成功的秘密。

sentences.en: Let's start with a quote from Daniel Presley.
sentences.zh: 让我们从 Daniel Presley 的一句话开始。

sentences.en: I'm sure many of you know who he is. He is a great dude.
sentences.zh: 我相信你们很多人都知道他是谁，他是个很棒的人。

sentences.en: The biggest leverage is no longer capital.
sentences.zh: 最大的杠杆不再是资本。

sentences.en: The biggest leverage is enterprise, the ability to run a great business.
sentences.zh: 最大的杠杆是企业，是经营一家伟大企业的能力。

sentences.en: And in particular, the biggest leverage is personal brand.
sentences.zh: 而尤其是，最大的杠杆是个人品牌。

sentences.en: Having a big audience.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个庞大的受众。

sentences.en: As soon as you've got enough people paying attention to you, you have this enormous form of leverage.
sentences.zh: 一旦有足够多的人关注你，你就拥有了一种巨大的杠杆。

sentences.en: And the reason this is, is because the rules of wealth creation have fundamentally changed.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，财富创造的规则已经从根本上改变了。

sentences.en: The assets that drove income in the industrial age, like property, factories, machinery, physical goods are being replaced by digital assets, audience, personal brand, IP, content, data, software that are incredibly cheap to build, more scalable, harder to tax and compound while you sleep.
sentences.zh: 工业时代驱动收入的资产，比如房产、工厂、机器、实体商品，正在被数字资产取代——受众、个人品牌、IP、内容、数据、软件，这些东西建造成本极低，扩展性更强，更难被征税，而且在你睡觉时也在不断复利增长。

sentences.en: The only requirement to building leverage for yourself in today's world is a good idea, and the confidence to post it on the internet.
sentences.zh: 在今天这个世界，为自己建立杠杆的唯一条件，就是一个好想法，以及把它发到互联网上的信心。

sentences.en: The problem, and where the opportunity lies is that most people are still conditioned by industrial values.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，也是机会所在，大多数人的思维仍然被工业时代的价值观所束缚。

sentences.en: They still think for some reason that going to school, getting a job, and retiring at some age is the safe and secure route when it's the least safe and secure route.
sentences.zh: 他们不知为何仍然认为，上学、找份工作、到某个年龄退休是一条安全稳妥的路，而实际上那是最不安全、最不稳妥的路。

sentences.en: And the same holds true for building leverage for yourself, for increasing your ability to generate wealth.
sentences.zh: 同样的道理也适用于为自己建立杠杆、提升创造财富的能力。

sentences.en: Old leverage comes from physical, tangible assets.
sentences.zh: 旧杠杆来自实体的、有形的资产。

sentences.en: So you can think of house, a factory, a Rolex, a fleet of trucks, a warehouse of inventory or gold.
sentences.zh: 你可以想想房子、工厂、劳力士、卡车车队、一仓库的库存或者黄金。

sentences.en: You buy them and then let them appreciate or generate income.
sentences.zh: 你买下它们，然后让它们升值或产生收入。

sentences.en: Old leverage is linear and local, so a factory can only produce so many units per day, and a house can only be rented to one tenant at a time.
sentences.zh: 旧杠杆是线性的、本地化的，一家工厂每天只能生产那么多件产品，一套房子一次只能租给一个租客。

sentences.en: Now, don't get me wrong leverages leverage, and old leverage can be a very good thing.
sentences.zh: 别误会，杠杆就是杠杆，旧杠杆也可以是非常好的东西。

sentences.en: But most people, especially beginners, just don't have the capital to invest in these assets.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人，尤其是新手，根本没有资本去投资这些资产。

sentences.en: You're probably not going to buy real estate anytime soon if you're in thousands of dollars of student debt, and you probably won't buy a Rolex until your business does increasingly well.
sentences.zh: 如果你还背着几千美元的学生贷款，你短期内大概不会去买房产，在你的生意做得相当好之前，你大概也不会去买劳力士。

sentences.en: And that's the beautiful thing about living in today's world, is that leverage is no longer available to only those with capital.
sentences.zh: 而这正是生活在当今世界的美妙之处——杠杆不再只属于那些有资本的人。

sentences.en: And the other important thing is that physical assets are going to be the first thing that governments find, tax and seize if wages collapse, which is more likely today than yesterday, because AI can swiftly do that, leading to governments expanding social safety nets.
sentences.zh: 另一个重点是，如果工资崩溃，实体资产将是政府最先发现、征税和没收的东西，而今天工资崩溃的可能性比昨天更大，因为AI可以迅速做到这一点，导致政府扩大社会安全网。

sentences.en: Governments are much less likely to seize an email list of 1000 to 10,000 people, or a library of content, or a best selling book.
sentences.zh: 政府没收一个1000到10000人的邮件列表、一个内容库或者一本畅销书的可能性要小得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can sell your house for $100,000, but you can also just send a well-written email to your email list and make 10 to $100,000 if you know what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 没错，你可以卖掉你的房子拿到10万美元，但你也可以给你的邮件列表发一封写得很好的邮件，赚到1万到10万美元，前提是你知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: New leverage comes from intangible digital assets, so an audience, personal brand, IP data systems or software, these are the leverage of the newly rich media data and code.
sentences.zh: 新杠杆来自无形的数字资产，也就是受众、个人品牌、IP、数据系统或软件，这些是新富阶层的杠杆——媒体、数据和代码。

sentences.en: Content can be written once and seen by millions of people.
sentences.zh: 内容可以写一次，被数百万人看到。

sentences.en: Software can be created once and serve millions of users.
sentences.zh: 软件可以创建一次，服务数百万用户。

sentences.en: The things that you use every day, social media and apps or software.
sentences.zh: 你每天都在用的东西，社交媒体、App或软件。

sentences.en: The things that are becoming more accessible to you to actually create and build.
sentences.zh: 这些东西对你来说正变得越来越容易去创造和构建。

sentences.en: You're watching people build leverage in real time for their future, doing something meaningful most of the time.
sentences.zh: 你正在实时看着别人为自己的未来建立杠杆，而且大多数时候他们做的是有意义的事。

sentences.en: And for most people, writing is the most accessible and practical form of leverage.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，写作是最容易上手、最实用的杠杆形式。

sentences.en: You can learn to code, but if you cannot attract people to care about the product you built, then nobody will use or pay for it.
sentences.zh: 你可以学编程，但如果你无法吸引人们关心你做的产品，那就没人会用，也没人会付钱。

sentences.en: Writing is the leverage that unlocks other forms of leverage.
sentences.zh: 写作是解锁其他杠杆形式的杠杆。

sentences.en: Everything you see is essentially writing.
sentences.zh: 你看到的一切本质上都是写作。

sentences.en: You have social media, captions, DM's or messages, advertising, social posts, emails, web page copy, video scripts, articles.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体、文案、私信或消息、广告、社交帖子、邮件、网页文案、视频脚本、文章。

sentences.en: That's the other thing is, even if you want to do video in the future, but you don't have the time to edit when you're not confident enough to be in front of the camera yet, start writing, because then you'll have a backlog of scripts that you can use, or you'll just be so much better at grabbing attention than the next person.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，即使你将来想做视频，但你目前没时间剪辑，或者还没有足够的信心出镜，那就从写作开始，因为这样你就会积累一堆可以用的脚本，或者你抓取注意力的能力会比下一个人强得多。

sentences.en: And when you do start creating videos, you're going to be miles ahead of the people who didn't practice articulating or organizing their thoughts on paper through writing.
sentences.zh: 当你真的开始做视频的时候，你会远远领先那些没有通过写作在纸上练习表达和组织想法的人。

sentences.en: And if you can build an audience on a writing platform like X, Substack, threads, etc. even Instagram, all of my posts are just written posts in the form of an image.
sentences.zh: 如果你能在一个写作平台上建立受众，比如X、Substack、Threads等等，甚至Instagram也行——我所有的帖子本质上都是图片形式的文字帖。

sentences.en: Then when it comes time for you to get on YouTube or do a podcast, or do other things like that, you have an audience already built that you can say, hey, here's my YouTube, here are my videos, and then your audience grows so much faster on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 那么当你要开始做YouTube或者播客，或者做其他类似的事情时，你已经有了一个现成的受众，你可以跟他们说，嘿，这是我的YouTube频道，这是我的视频，然后你的YouTube受众增长速度会快得多。

sentences.en: That's exactly what I did.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And I'm just an introvert.
sentences.zh: 而且我就是个内向的人。

sentences.en: It's so much more appealing to just sit down and enjoy the creative process of writing for 1 to 2 hours every morning while sleeping well, knowing that it is essentially fueling my entire business and life's work or whatever kind of work I want to do.
sentences.zh: 每天早上坐下来享受一到两小时的写作创作过程，同时睡得好好的，知道这本质上是在为我的整个事业和人生事业——或者说我想做的任何工作——提供燃料，这吸引力要大得多。

sentences.en: The other thing is that you won't see these digital assets on a business balance sheet, but they represent 90% of the S&P 500 value.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，你不会在企业的资产负债表上看到这些数字资产，但它们代表了标普500指数90%的价值。

sentences.en: Kim Kardashian, Taylor Swift, Ryan Reynolds, Mr. Beast, Elon Musk all have massive audiences and personal brands, but you probably don't want anything near their level of fame, and that's perfectly fine because you don't need millions of followers to make this work.
sentences.zh: Kim Kardashian、Taylor Swift、Ryan Reynolds、Mr. Beast、Elon Musk都拥有庞大的受众和个人品牌，但你大概率根本不想达到他们那种知名度，这完全没问题，因为你不需要几百万粉丝才能做成这件事。

sentences.en: This is like one big thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的误区。

sentences.en: When I talk to beginner creators, they think it's they have millions of followers or they have nothing.
sentences.zh: 当我和新手创作者聊天时，他们觉得要么有几百万粉丝，要么就什么都没有。

sentences.en: Personally, I replaced my freelancing income at around 5000 followers.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我在大约5000粉丝的时候就替代了我的自由职业收入。

sentences.en: My buddy Randy is a fitness personal trainer and at 10,000 followers, he was making well over $100,000 a month because again, he knew what he was doing.
sentences.zh: 我朋友Randy是个健身私人教练，在10000粉丝的时候，他每月收入远超10万美元，因为他知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: He studied, he invested in his education.
sentences.zh: 他学习，他投资自己的教育。

sentences.en: He learned the skill of business and marketing and sales that allowed him to do that.
sentences.zh: 他学会了商业、营销和销售的技能，这让他能做到这一点。

sentences.en: People hear that, oh, $100,000 a month, and they think that's absolutely absurd.
sentences.zh: 人们听到这个，哦，一个月10万美元，觉得这简直荒谬。

sentences.en: That's on the low end for business.
sentences.zh: 这在商业里算是低的了。

sentences.en: Like you're still in this employee mindset of I get paid for my time, not my value.
sentences.zh: 你仍然停留在那种员工思维里，觉得我是按时间获得报酬，而不是按价值。

sentences.en: And you have a poor relationship with money that changes how you perceive it.
sentences.zh: 而且你跟金钱的关系很糟糕，这改变了你感知金钱的方式。

sentences.en: And so you hear $100,000 and you think that's not even close to possible for me.
sentences.zh: 所以你听到10万美元，就觉得这对我来说连边都沾不上。

sentences.en: And that's completely fine because you probably don't need that much.
sentences.zh: 这完全没关系，因为你大概率不需要那么多。

sentences.en: And as I said, that's on the low end for like a business that's doing well.
sentences.zh: 而且我说了，对于一个做得好的生意来说，这算是低的了。

sentences.en: So if you just want to replace your income, that's not far off.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你只是想替代你的收入，那并不遥远。

sentences.en: That's three to 6 to 12 months of focused learning and effort and skill acquisition and showing up every day and actually putting your thoughts out there and trying to grow.
sentences.zh: 那是三到六个月、最多十二个月的专注学习、努力、技能获取，每天出现，真正把你的想法发布出去，并尝试增长。

sentences.en: The point is that people drastically overestimate how much is actually required for them to win.
sentences.zh: 重点是，人们严重高估了他们真正需要多少才能赢。

sentences.en: And so they psych themselves out.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把自己吓退了。

sentences.en: They get paralyzed.
sentences.zh: 他们陷入瘫痪。

sentences.en: Analysis by paralysis a paralysis by analysis.
sentences.zh: 分析导致瘫痪，瘫痪导致分析。

sentences.en: Because all they see is these out of touch celebrities and influencers with millions of followers, because that's all they follow.
sentences.zh: 因为他们看到的全是那些脱离现实的、有几百万粉丝的名人和网红，因为他们只关注这些人。

sentences.en: So I'd be stupid if I didn't mention this here, but that's exactly why we run the Creator Bootcamp, where you turn your interest into an audience that pays you.
sentences.zh: 所以我要是不在这里提一下就太蠢了，但这正是我们运营Creator Bootcamp的原因，在那里你把你的兴趣变成愿意为你付费的受众。

sentences.en: You walk away with clarity on the topics that you can talk about, a content system that runs on 60 minutes a day, and one idea that becomes a week of content.
sentences.zh: 你会带着清晰的认知离开，知道你可以谈论什么话题，拥有一个每天只需60分钟运转的内容系统，以及一个能变成一周内容的想法。

sentences.en: General enrollment for this is closed, but it is still available for those who sign up for Eden on the Pro plan.
sentences.zh: 这个训练营的常规报名已经关闭了，但对于注册Eden专业版计划的人来说仍然可以参加。

sentences.en: So if you want to join a community of other creators that are doing the same thing as you and learn everything that you need to start, then check it out with the link in the description or go to Enzo Slash Bootcamp.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想加入一个由其他和你在做同样事情的创作者组成的社区，并学习你起步所需的一切，那就去看看描述里的链接，或者去Enzo Slash Bootcamp。

sentences.en: Now the next thing I want to talk about is how writing completely shifts your brain and your life.
sentences.zh: 现在我想聊的下一件事是，写作如何彻底改变你的大脑和你的生活。

sentences.en: And this is super hard to explain, but writing goes so much deeper than just putting your pen to paper and like, drawing little scribbles.
sentences.zh: 这超级难解释，但写作远比只是把笔放在纸上、画些小涂鸦要深刻得多。

sentences.en: Obviously, it shifts your mind to see the world in a more meaningful way.
sentences.zh: 显然，它转变你的思维，让你以一种更有意义的方式看待世界。

sentences.en: You make more connections, you receive more good dopamine.
sentences.zh: 你建立更多的连接，你获得更多好的多巴胺。

sentences.en: Through those connections, you notice more in the world.
sentences.zh: 通过这些连接，你在世界中注意到更多东西。

sentences.en: Conversations become a source of inspiration.
sentences.zh: 对话变成了灵感的来源。

sentences.en: Your thoughts become filled with ideas you're wrestling to understand.
sentences.zh: 你的思绪里会充满你正在努力理解的想法。

sentences.en: You notice more detail in life rather than living on the stressful surface.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到生活中更多的细节，而不是活在充满压力的表面。

sentences.en: And so, in my eyes, there are four key benefits to writing.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我看来，写作有四个核心好处。

sentences.en: The first is that writing rewires how you think, and the core mechanism here is forced linearity, which is just a fancy way of saying that you can feel like you understand something in your head, but writing forces you to collapse it into a single stream.
sentences.zh: 第一，写作会重塑你的思维方式，其核心机制是"强制线性化"——说白了就是，你脑子里可能觉得自己懂了某件事，但写作会迫使你把那些想法压缩成一条单一的思路。

sentences.en: Thinking without writing is like walking through a forest where you can see every direction.
sentences.zh: 不写作的思考，就像在一片你能看到四面八方的森林里行走。

sentences.en: While writing itself is like driving on a road through the disorienting mess, you have to decide where you're going, which turns you're going to make, and whether or not you want to take the scenic route and how to navigate back if you get lost.
sentences.zh: 而写作本身，就像在令人迷失的混乱中沿着一条路开车，你必须决定要去哪里、要拐哪些弯、要不要走风景路线，以及迷路了怎么绕回来。

sentences.en: In other words, writing is the apparatus for thinking it's the gym where your mind is built.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，写作是思考的工具，是塑造你心智的健身房。

sentences.en: So those who are very into health and fitness and go to the gym to strengthen their body and make sure it's healthy, but you're not writing for your mind, you need to make that connection so you may feel like you understand your feelings or the counterarguments going on in your head, or even your own values and beliefs, but you actually write them out.
sentences.zh: 那些热衷于健康和健身、去健身房锻炼身体、确保身体健康的人，如果你不为自己的心智写作，你需要建立这种关联——你可能觉得自己理解自己的感受、脑子里那些互相矛盾的声音，甚至自己的价值观和信念，但当你真正把它们写出来时。

sentences.en: I can almost guarantee that you don't understand those things, and that someone else either planted it in your head.
sentences.zh: 我几乎可以保证，你并不理解那些东西，而且很可能是别人把它们植入你脑中的。

sentences.en: You adopted beliefs and ideologies without question, and now they're dominating your mind and taking control of your life.
sentences.zh: 你不加质疑地接受了那些信念和意识形态，现在它们正主宰着你的思想，掌控着你的人生。

sentences.en: And yes, it is that serious.
sentences.zh: 没错，事情就是这么严重。

sentences.en: Now, benefit number two is that writing increases pattern recognition and therefore it increases dopamine good dopamine.
sentences.zh: 第二个好处是，写作能提升模式识别能力，从而增加多巴胺——好的多巴胺。

sentences.en: And there are a few layers to this.
sentences.zh: 这里面有几个层次。

sentences.en: The first is that by writing regularly you build an external record of your thinking, you are able to quickly reference what you've written in the past as a way of articulating your current thoughts better.
sentences.zh: 第一层是，通过定期写作，你建立了一个自己思考的外部记录，你能快速参考过去写下的东西，从而更好地表达当前的想法。

sentences.en: It helps you think with clarity. And I'm not talking.
sentences.zh: 它能帮你清晰地思考。我不是在说。

sentences.en: You actually go and reference the thing I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 你真的去翻看我说过的东西。

sentences.en: Since you wrote it down, since you wrote the newsletter or the article, or even just the journal entry that is now more of a part of your mind, and you're able to say those things in a more clear way.
sentences.zh: 因为你把它写下来了，因为你写了 newsletter 或文章，甚至只是日记，它现在更深刻地成为你心智的一部分，你就能更清晰地表达那些东西。

sentences.en: Now, the second layer is similar to what's called the photographer's eye.
sentences.zh: 第二层类似于所谓的"摄影师之眼"。

sentences.en: So for a photographer, after a few years of serious practice, you start to see frames and compositions in everyday life so the world doesn't look the same.
sentences.zh: 对于一个摄影师来说，经过几年认真的练习后，你开始能在日常生活中看到画面和构图，世界看起来就不一样了。

sentences.en: Because you go to a mountain range, you're on a hike, and then you can see something that other people can't. You start to compose the scene in your mind, like you were taking a picture, and you start to think and appreciate the scenery that much more.
sentences.zh: 因为你走到一片山脉，你在徒步，然后你能看到别人看不到的东西。你开始在脑海中构图，就像在拍照一样，你开始更深入地思考和欣赏眼前的风景。

sentences.en: With writing.
sentences.zh: 写作也一样。

sentences.en: You notice this when you're speaking with other people, when you're having a conversation in other people's writing, in the books you read, it opens up a deeper appreciation for the art in your life.
sentences.zh: 当你和别人交谈时，当你在别人的文字里、在你读的书里，你会注意到这一点，它会让你对生活中的艺术产生更深层的欣赏。

sentences.en: Now, the third layer is that you notice ideas you normally wouldn't have, and this is just how the mind works.
sentences.zh: 第三层是，你会注意到那些你原本不会有的想法，这就是心智运作的方式。

sentences.en: But when you have a goal or a project that you're working towards, your mind kind of conspires in your favor, so to say psycho cybernetics.
sentences.zh: 当你有一个目标或正在推进一个项目时，你的心智会以某种方式"密谋"来帮助你，用心理控制论的话来说。

sentences.en: It notices the things that are going to aid you in achieving your goal.
sentences.zh: 它会注意到那些有助于你实现目标的事物。

sentences.en: The problem is that most people have unconscious goals.
sentences.zh: 问题是，大多数人只有无意识的目标。

sentences.en: They haven't made their goals conscious, or they haven't set their own meaningful goals that actually trump the unconscious goals.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把自己的目标变成有意识的，或者他们没有设定自己真正有意义的、能压倒无意识目标的目标。

sentences.en: Many people set conscious goals, but they're unconscious goals that other people set for them are still more conditioned into their brain, so their conscious goals don't really mean anything.
sentences.zh: 很多人设定了有意识的目标，但别人为他们设定的无意识目标，在他们脑中仍然被更深地条件化了，所以他们那些有意识的目标其实毫无意义。

sentences.en: There's no gravity to them, and you let them go immediately.
sentences.zh: 那些目标没有引力，你会立刻放弃它们。

sentences.en: That's what most New Year's resolutions are.
sentences.zh: 大多数新年决心就是这样。

sentences.en: But for someone who has been conditioned since childhood that they should go to school and be a good student, the idea of starting a business isn't even going to register in their brain because it's a threat to who they are.
sentences.zh: 但对于一个从小就被条件化、认为应该上学、做个好学生的人来说，"创业"这个想法甚至不会在他们脑中浮现，因为那是对他们自我身份的威胁。

sentences.en: They're going to notice the ideas and the opportunities that allow them to advance through the traditional school job retire path.
sentences.zh: 他们会注意到那些能让他们沿着"上学-工作-退休"这条传统路径前进的想法和机会。

sentences.en: That's just how it works.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: It's the same phenomenon where if you take me and take you and we read the same book, different ideas are going to stick out to us, and we're going to see different ideas as more important, and we're going to remember them.
sentences.zh: 这跟以下现象是一样的：如果你和我读同一本书，不同的想法会吸引我们，我们会认为不同的想法更重要，并且记住它们。

sentences.en: We're essentially going to read two entirely different books just by how we interpret it.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上会因为解读方式的不同，而读出两本完全不同的书。

sentences.en: And that is all because of the goals and projects that are framing how we perceive situations.
sentences.zh: 这完全是因为我们心中的目标和项目，在框定我们感知一切的方式。

sentences.en: So for me, I have a newsletter that I write every single week that turns into this YouTube video and turns into other content, but that is my sole focus.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我每周都会写一份 newsletter，它会变成这期 YouTube 视频，也会变成其他内容，而这就是我唯一的焦点。

sentences.en: That is the important goal for my week.
sentences.zh: 这就是我这一周最重要的目标。

sentences.en: And so when I go and walks or I listen to conversations, ideas just pop up out of nowhere and somehow connect themselves to my newsletter.
sentences.zh: 所以当我去散步，或者听别人聊天时，各种想法就会凭空冒出来，并且莫名其妙地自动和我的 newsletter 连接在一起。

sentences.en: And that's how my newsletters and writing become very unique is because I'm not just sitting down and writing it all at once.
sentences.zh: 我的 newsletter 和写作之所以能变得非常独特，就是因为我并不是坐下来一口气写完的。

sentences.en: They're I'm collecting ideas just by living my life.
sentences.zh: 我只是在过自己的生活时，不断收集想法。

sentences.en: Since I have the newsletter as a top of mind goal, your mind is like a heat seeking missile toward its goals, but you actually need goals, or else you're going to be a heat seeking missile toward the goals that society assigned for you.
sentences.zh: 因为我把 newsletter 当作一个时刻放在心上的目标，你的大脑就像一颗追踪目标的寻热导弹，但你必须真的有目标，否则你就会变成一颗追踪社会指派目标的寻热导弹。

sentences.en: And that's horrible.
sentences.zh: 而那太可怕了。

sentences.en: So writing is one way out of that mess, because you actually have a project to focus your mind on.
sentences.zh: 所以写作是逃离那团乱麻的一条路，因为你终于有了一个项目，能让你的大脑聚焦。

sentences.en: That's actually the entire learning process as well.
sentences.zh: 这其实也是整个学习过程的核心。

sentences.en: That's how you learn most things.
sentences.zh: 你学大多数东西都是这样学的。

sentences.en: So benefit number three is that writing helps you articulate your thoughts as we've touched on.
sentences.zh: 第三个好处是，写作能帮你清晰表达想法，这一点我们已经提到了。

sentences.en: But most people walk around believing they understand things that they don't, not because they're dumb, but because they've never been forced to externalize the thought and actually look at it.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人每天走来走去，都以为自己懂一些其实根本不懂的东西，不是因为他们笨，而是因为他们从来没有被迫把想法外化出来，真正审视它。

sentences.en: Writing is not only a tool to improve communication, thus improving most other areas of your life, but a tool to expose whether or not you actually know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 写作不仅是一个改善沟通的工具，从而改善你生活的大多数领域，它还是一个能暴露你到底知不知道自己在说什么的工具。

sentences.en: And that's what most people are afraid of when it comes to writing.
sentences.zh: 而这正是大多数人在面对写作时最害怕的东西。

sentences.en: They're afraid of the struggle that comes from doing something meaningful.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕做有意义的事情时，必然会遇到的那种挣扎。

sentences.en: They just want to coast by and enjoy their life and hopefully make some money, even though they're not putting much effort into it.
sentences.zh: 他们只想轻松混过去，享受生活，然后希望能赚点钱，尽管他们并没有投入多少努力。

sentences.en: And of course, they end up in a mediocre life because they're running on autopilot.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们最终会过上平庸的生活，因为他们一直在自动驾驶。

sentences.en: They don't choose their struggle again, their assign, their struggle.
sentences.zh: 他们没有选择自己的挣扎，而是被分配了挣扎。

sentences.en: They want the writing or the creative work to be easy.
sentences.zh: 他们希望写作或者创造性工作能轻松一点。

sentences.en: They want all of the ideas to just come to their head immediately.
sentences.zh: 他们希望所有想法能立刻自动出现在脑子里。

sentences.en: They don't want to sit down and stare at a blank page and be forced to research and learn and find what their actual beliefs are so they can write it out.
sentences.zh: 他们不想坐下来，盯着一张白纸，被迫去研究、去学习、去找到自己真正的信念，然后才能写出来。

sentences.en: And that leads to the important next benefit, which is that writing helps you learn faster, and the future belongs to those who can learn the fastest.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了下一个重要的好处：写作能帮你学得更快，而未来属于那些学得最快的人。

sentences.en: Because if the gap between where you are and where you want to be is knowledge, is learning is understanding how to do the things that gets the result of the person you want to be.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你和你想成为的人之间的差距，是知识，是学习，是理解如何做成那些能带来结果的事。

sentences.en: Then the person that learns fastest is the one who gets to that point the fastest.
sentences.zh: 那么学得最快的那个人，就是最快到达那个位置的人。

sentences.en: The person who doesn't learn at all.
sentences.zh: 而完全不学习的人。

sentences.en: After graduation, which is what most people do, they go to school, they graduate, and then they never learn a thing again.
sentences.zh: 毕业之后，大多数人就是这样，他们上学、毕业，然后这辈子再也没学过任何东西。

sentences.en: For the rest of their life.
sentences.zh: 在他们的余生里。

sentences.en: They're just going off of their pre-set knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在吃自己预设好的老本。

sentences.en: Writing is the antidote to that because 80% of writing is research and learning.
sentences.zh: 写作就是解药，因为写作的 80% 是研究和学习。

sentences.en: Writing is both a form of teaching and understanding.
sentences.zh: 写作既是一种教学形式，也是一种理解形式。

sentences.en: In learning science, there's the protégé effect, which shows that students who teach material retain a better than students who merely study it.
sentences.zh: 在学习科学里，有一个“门徒效应”，它表明，教别人材料的学生，比那些只是自己学的学生，掌握得更好。

sentences.en: The cognitive load required to figure out how to explain something to someone else forces deeper understanding, better organization, and identification of gaps in knowledge.
sentences.zh: 为了想清楚如何向别人解释某件事，所需要的认知负荷，会迫使你更深入地理解、更好地组织信息，并识别出知识上的漏洞。

sentences.en: I'm not exaggerating when I say that I learned more in six months of writing when I started out, than I did throughout the entirety of college or the entirety of high school.
sentences.zh: 毫不夸张地说，我刚开始写作那六个月学到的东西，比我整个大学和整个高中加起来都多。

sentences.en: And I'm not talking about, like, learning basic English and learning how to write letters on a page.
sentences.zh: 我说的不是学基础英语、学怎么在纸上写字那种东西。

sentences.en: I didn't really need to learn basic history because I wasn't that interested in it.
sentences.zh: 我其实不需要学基础历史，因为我对它没那么感兴趣。

sentences.en: I didn't even apply myself and learn it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都没认真去学。

sentences.en: And now, since I chose to write about history in some of my newsletters, I and I understand it so much better than I did just sitting in a lecture at school.
sentences.zh: 而现在，因为我在一些 newsletter 里选择写历史话题，我对它的理解比当年坐在学校讲座里要深得多。

sentences.en: You look at Daniel Berger, who talks about this quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 你看看 Daniel Berger，他经常聊这个。

sentences.en: He didn't go to school.
sentences.zh: 他没上过学。

sentences.en: His parents taught him how to read, how to write, and how to just generally operate within society according to their values.
sentences.zh: 他父母教他阅读、写作，以及如何按照他们的价值观在社会中正常生活。

sentences.en: But outside of that, learning is the process of life.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，学习就是生活的过程。

sentences.en: Learning is what you do when you're actually pursuing something meaningful and building something meaningful.
sentences.zh: 学习是你真正追求有意义的东西、构建有意义的东西时所做的事。

sentences.en: You learn what you need to learn and you become ten times more articulate when you do it that way.
sentences.zh: 你学你需要学的，用这种方式你会变得十倍善于表达。

sentences.en: Lastly, writing demands that you understand.
sentences.zh: 最后，写作要求你真正理解。

sentences.en: So you read something, you feel like you get it.
sentences.zh: 你读了点东西，觉得自己懂了。

sentences.en: Then you try to write about it and you realize that you can't. And most people think it's because they aren't qualified to write about the topic, which is bullshit.
sentences.zh: 然后你试着写出来，才发现你写不出来。大多数人以为这是因为自己没资格写这个话题，这纯属扯淡。

sentences.en: You can write about an idea just like any other person on planet Earth can, just like you can speak it to your friend right now.
sentences.zh: 你可以写一个想法，就像地球上任何一个人都可以写一样，就像你现在可以跟朋友讲出来一样。

sentences.en: You can go and tell your friend about the idea that you heard about.
sentences.zh: 你可以去跟朋友讲你听到的那个想法。

sentences.en: If you can do that, you can write about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你能做到那个，你就能写出来。

sentences.en: That's a limiting beliefs that stops so many creators and writers when it's just nonsense.
sentences.zh: 这是一种限制性信念，拦住了无数创作者和写作者，而这根本就是胡扯。

sentences.en: You're just creating invisible gatekeepers in your head out of fear of actually doing the thing and publishing your thoughts.
sentences.zh: 你只是出于恐惧，在自己脑子里造出了无形的守门人，害怕真正去做、去发布你的想法。

sentences.en: But that's actually a good thing, is not knowing how to write it, because you don't truly understand it, because that exposes the gap, and it gives you the thing to learn next that you would have never found if you didn't try to write what you had learned.
sentences.zh: 但这其实是好事，不知道怎么写，说明你没有真正理解它，因为这暴露了你的知识缺口，而且给了你下一步要学的东西——如果你不试着把学到的东西写出来，你永远找不到这个缺口。

sentences.en: Now we're going to talk about the writing system that I use to generate ideas people can't help but read, and I'm going to go over my general system.
sentences.zh: 现在我们聊聊我用来生成那些让人忍不住想读的想法的写作系统，我会过一遍我的整体系统。

sentences.en: This isn't going to be a course.
sentences.zh: 这不是一门课程。

sentences.en: I have plenty of other videos, plenty of resources.
sentences.zh: 我有很多其他视频，很多资源。

sentences.en: The boot camp, like I mentioned, if you want the full step by step process and all of the theory and the slides and all of the information you need along with the practices, then go and find it elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 就像我提到的，那个训练营，如果你想要完整的逐步操作流程、所有理论、幻灯片、所有你需要的信息以及练习，去别处找它。

sentences.en: This is a broad overview to just see if you're even interested in it.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个概览，让你看看自己是否真的感兴趣。

sentences.en: Now, when it comes to ideas, I've never been the most organized person.
sentences.zh: 说到想法，我从来不是最有条理的人。

sentences.en: I actually think building a second brain or a system for your ideas is like a false god.
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得，为你的想法构建一个第二大脑或系统，就像拜假神。

sentences.en: Because systems succumb to entropy, they fall apart with time.
sentences.zh: 因为系统会屈服于熵增，它们会随着时间瓦解。

sentences.en: It's always going to happen.
sentences.zh: 这一定会发生。

sentences.en: I don't care how perfect your notion system is for capturing ideas, it's going to fall apart one day.
sentences.zh: 我不管你的 Notion 系统捕捉想法有多完美，它总有一天会崩掉。

sentences.en: It's so cool to you right now.
sentences.zh: 你现在觉得它酷毙了。

sentences.en: It's not going to be in a year. You're going to grow up.
sentences.zh: 一年后就不会了。你会成长。

sentences.en: You're going to evolve.
sentences.zh: 你会进化。

sentences.en: You're going to try a new system, and then the same thing is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 你会尝试一个新系统，然后同样的事情会再次发生。

sentences.en: So just get over it.
sentences.zh: 所以，别纠结了。

sentences.en: Embrace the mess. Embrace the chaos.
sentences.zh: 拥抱混乱，拥抱混沌。

sentences.en: That's where I've honestly found the most success is just embracing the chaos, which doesn't have to be completely chaos and just jotting ideas down in the same place.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我最大的突破就来自拥抱混沌——它不必是完全无序，只是把想法随手记在同一个地方。

sentences.en: Just having a place where I can put ideas down so that at least they're recorded somewhere.
sentences.zh: 只要有一个地方能让我把想法放下来，至少它们被记录下来了。

sentences.en: And of course, ideas get lost all the time.
sentences.zh: 当然，想法随时会丢。

sentences.en: I can't find them all the time because that's not really the problem.
sentences.zh: 我也不是每次都能找到，但这其实不是问题所在。

sentences.en: If you need to remember it, then it's not important.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要刻意记住它，那它就不重要。

sentences.en: And if it's important, you'll remember it.
sentences.zh: 如果它真的重要，你自然会记住。

sentences.en: The act of writing it down is just the act of putting your thoughts into words.
sentences.zh: 写下来的动作，本身就是把思考变成文字的过程。

sentences.en: So I've found that great writing or content on the internet that actually gains traction and doesn't disappear into a black hole of nobody caring about your work, boils down to a few things.
sentences.zh: 我发现，那些真正能获得关注、不会消失在无人问津的黑洞里的好内容，归根结底就几个要素。

sentences.en: You need one topic or theme for the week that for me, that's my newsletter.
sentences.zh: 你需要一个每周的主题——对我来说，就是我的 newsletter。

sentences.en: You need a place to quickly jot down ideas.
sentences.zh: 你需要一个能快速记下想法的地方。

sentences.en: You need a way to capture inspiration.
sentences.zh: 你需要一种捕捉灵感的方式。

sentences.en: So social posts, YouTube videos, Substack articles, etc. PDFs, images.
sentences.zh: 比如社交帖子、YouTube 视频、Substack 文章等等，PDF、图片。

sentences.en: You need to understand how to package the hooker title so that people actually want to read it.
sentences.zh: 你需要懂得如何包装标题，让人们真的想点进去读。

sentences.en: Because writing or content is like a gift.
sentences.zh: 因为写作或内容就像一份礼物。

sentences.en: You have the actual contents, which is what you want to say.
sentences.zh: 你有实际的内容，那是你想说的话。

sentences.en: Then you have the packaging, what makes other people want to open it and see what's inside.
sentences.zh: 然后你有包装，那是让别人想打开看看里面有什么的东西。

sentences.en: And lastly, you need to effectively pull from your ideas, inspiration, and research while you're actually writing or creating because that's why you jot down the ideas in the first place is to reference them while you're writing.
sentences.zh: 最后，你在实际写作或创作时，需要能有效地调取你的想法、灵感和研究资料——这才是你一开始记下想法的原因，为了写作时能回头参考。

sentences.en: So my system is just that and we're going to go over it.
sentences.zh: 我的系统就是这样，我们一步步来看。

sentences.en: So the first step is how to pick what to write about.
sentences.zh: 第一步，如何选择写什么。

sentences.en: And this one always throws everyone for a loop because they just want to.
sentences.zh: 这一步总是让所有人卡住，因为他们只想——

sentences.en: They've been told to niche down.
sentences.zh: 他们一直被告诉要细分定位。

sentences.en: They don't know what to talk about.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道该聊什么。

sentences.en: They're afraid to talk about multiple things, even though they have multiple interests.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕聊多个话题，尽管他们有多个兴趣。

sentences.en: And if they have multiple interests, almost every other human being on the planet can have multiple interests.
sentences.zh: 而如果他们有多个兴趣，这个星球上几乎每个人都可以有多个兴趣。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not only interested in business, neither is any other businessman on the planet. They can.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不只对商业感兴趣，地球上任何一个商人也都不只对商业感兴趣。

sentences.en: People can become interested in something.
sentences.zh: 人是可以对一件事产生兴趣的。

sentences.en: Stop limiting yourself to what you can talk about if you find it important.
sentences.zh: 别再限制自己能聊什么了，只要你觉得它重要。

sentences.en: That's unique because you interpreted it and decided to post it.
sentences.zh: 那就是独特之处，因为你解读了它，并决定把它发出来。

sentences.en: That is all the niching down you need because you are not an animal that dies when they get put into a different niche or environment, like a lion that gets put in Alaska, you are a human who learns, builds and adapts so that they can thrive in any niche.
sentences.zh: 这就是你需要的全部"细分定位"——因为你又不是一种被放进不同生态位就会死的动物，比如一头被扔到阿拉斯加的狮子。你是一个人，你会学习、构建和适应，从而在任何生态位中茁壮成长。

sentences.en: So I operate by two principles when I pick a topic.
sentences.zh: 所以我在选主题时遵循两个原则。

sentences.en: First, is it something that I find important or worth sharing?
sentences.zh: 第一，这是我觉得重要或值得分享的东西吗？

sentences.en: Because by simply filtering an idea through my perspective and not overthinking myself to death, it becomes unique.
sentences.zh: 因为只要把一个想法经过我的视角过滤，并且不把自己纠结到死，它就变得独一无二。

sentences.en: I have a specific identity, and I'm probably not going to speak to soccer moms in their 40s, no matter how hard I try, by just talking about what I find worth sharing, it will attract the people I can impact the most.
sentences.zh: 我有自己特定的身份，不管我怎么努力，大概都没办法跟 40 岁的足球妈妈对话。我只聊我觉得值得分享的东西，它自然会吸引那些我能影响最深的人。

sentences.en: The second principle is is it packaged or framed in a way that grabs attention because as a writer, that's what you do.
sentences.zh: 第二个原则是，它有没有被包装或框定成一个能抓人眼球的方式，因为作为一个写作者，这就是你要做的事。

sentences.en: That's your job.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的工作。

sentences.en: There's journaling and then there's writing.
sentences.zh: 写日记是一回事，写作是另一回事。

sentences.en: You grab attention, otherwise your writing doesn't get read.
sentences.zh: 你得抓住注意力，否则你写的东西根本没人看。

sentences.en: The way you do that in today's world is by studying what's working on social media and applying the structure and principles to your hook, your title, your structure. ET cetera.
sentences.zh: 在今天这个世界里，做到这一点的方法就是去研究社交媒体上什么东西在奏效，然后把那些结构和原则用到你的钩子、标题、结构上，等等。

sentences.en: I'm subscribed to the Substack subreddit, and I got a notification the other day, and it was just a person that was complaining about their work not gaining traction, but they don't want to do what it takes to gain traction.
sentences.zh: 我订阅了 Substack 的 subreddit，前几天收到一条通知，就是一个人在抱怨自己的作品没有起色，但他们又不愿意去做那些能让作品起色的事。

sentences.en: They're like, oh, I love the writing.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，我就是爱写作。

sentences.en: I just love the writing aspect of it, but it's not picking up. Why is that?
sentences.zh: 我就是纯粹喜欢写作这件事本身，但就是火不起来，为什么会这样？

sentences.en: I don't want to conform my voice to these hooks or these structures or whatever it may be, but they can't see that they're contradicting themselves.
sentences.zh: 我不想让自己的声音去迎合这些钩子、这些结构或者不管什么东西，但他们看不到自己在自相矛盾。

sentences.en: They want to be a writer, but they don't care what people think, but they also want people to care about their writing.
sentences.zh: 他们想当写作者，却不在乎别人怎么想，但他们又希望别人在乎他们写的东西。

sentences.en: You have to understand that refining your voice for it to be impactful to other people is not sacrificing your authenticity or your voice.
sentences.zh: 你必须明白，打磨你的声音，让它能对别人产生冲击力，这不叫牺牲你的真实性或你的声音。

sentences.en: It's called improving your voice so that you become a better writer.
sentences.zh: 这叫精进你的声音，让你成为一个更好的写作者。

sentences.en: Before I go on a large tangent and rant, that's just social media growth in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 在我跑题太远、开始长篇大论之前，这基本上就是社交媒体增长的要点。

sentences.en: That's what you do.
sentences.zh: 这就是你要做的事。

sentences.en: And the simplest way to do this is to just research before you actually write the thing.
sentences.zh: 而最简单的做法，就是在你真正动笔之前先做研究。

sentences.en: Before you post the YouTube video, look at titles that work.
sentences.zh: 在你发布 YouTube 视频之前，去看看那些奏效的标题。

sentences.en: You need to expose yourself to what works over and over again, so that your pattern recognition system just knows what to write.
sentences.zh: 你需要反复地让自己接触那些奏效的东西，这样你的模式识别系统就会自然而然地知道该写什么。

sentences.en: Like it's second nature, you need to read good tweets.
sentences.zh: 就像第二天性一样，你需要去读好的推文。

sentences.en: Viral maybe not viral tweets, high performing tweets over and over.
sentences.zh: 爆款推文，也许不一定是爆款，但至少是表现很好的推文，反复地读。

sentences.en: You need to read more Substack articles that have done well and ask yourself, why did this do so well compared to mine, compared to the ones that didn't do well?
sentences.zh: 你需要去读更多做得好的 Substack 文章，然后问自己，为什么这篇做得这么好，跟我的比，跟那些没做好的比，差别在哪里？

sentences.en: You just have to study and learn.
sentences.zh: 你就是得去研究、去学习。

sentences.en: That's what that's what you do.
sentences.zh: 这就是你要做的事。

sentences.en: And what that does is it shows you and teaches you what the market is already paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 而这样做的作用是，它会向你展示、教会你市场已经在关注什么。

sentences.en: Because if you were to start a business, are you going to go and start something completely new?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你要开始一门生意，你会去搞一个完全没人做过的新东西吗？

sentences.en: You.
sentences.zh: 你。

sentences.en: I'm talking about you, not some special genius person.
sentences.zh: 我说的就是你，不是什么特别的天才人物。

sentences.en: Know what you do when you start a business is you do what works and you make it your own.
sentences.zh: 你要知道，当你开始一门生意的时候，你做的事就是去做那些已经被验证有效的东西，然后把它变成你自己的。

sentences.en: You can go and sell your productivity journal because people actually buy those, but you add your little spin to it.
sentences.zh: 你可以去卖你的效率手账，因为人们真的会买这些东西，但你给它加上一点你自己的独特风格。

sentences.en: It's exactly what you do with content.
sentences.zh: 做内容完全就是同一回事。

sentences.en: You do what works, but with your own spin, from your own voice, from your own interpretation.
sentences.zh: 你去做那些奏效的事，但加上你自己的风格，用你自己的声音，用你自己的解读。

sentences.en: So there are a few ways to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以有几种方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to show you how to do it in Eden.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我来给你演示怎么在 Eden 里做。

sentences.en: What I'm going to show you is free to do.
sentences.zh: 我要给你看的东西是免费的。

sentences.en: You don't have to pay to do any of this, but you can do it anywhere.
sentences.zh: 你不用花一分钱，随时随地都能做。

sentences.en: You can do it in notes and wherever you want to capture ideas to.
sentences.zh: 你可以在备忘录里做，在任何你想捕捉想法的地方做。

sentences.en: But you can paste links into your library and just store the ideas here on your phone to you.
sentences.zh: 你可以把链接粘贴到你的资料库里，把想法直接存在手机上。

sentences.en: Download the iOS app that's on test flight.
sentences.zh: 下载 TestFlight 上的 iOS 应用。

sentences.en: You hit the quick capture, you jot an idea down.
sentences.zh: 点一下快速捕捉，随手记下一个想法。

sentences.en: It comes in looking like this.
sentences.zh: 它进来的时候就是这个样子。

sentences.en: You can add as many as you want, and you can paste social links as well as you scroll and find them on the timeline.
sentences.zh: 你想加多少就加多少，刷时间线的时候看到社交链接也可以直接粘贴进去。

sentences.en: So that's the one way you do it is when you see a video that's doing really well or an idea that you want to save, you save it in a place where you can preferably find it later.
sentences.zh: 所以这是其中一种方式：当你看到一个表现很好的视频，或者一个你想保存的想法，就把它存到一个你之后能找到的地方。

sentences.en: But as I said, if it disappears, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 但就像我说的，如果它消失了，也没关系。

sentences.en: But then the next thing you can use is an outlier tool.
sentences.zh: 接下来你可以用的另一个东西是 outlier 工具。

sentences.en: So there are tools like one of ten that offers like you can look at what's trending on YouTube and there's others like that, but there's also the discover feed in Eden.
sentences.zh: 比如像 1of10 这样的工具，可以让你看到 YouTube 上什么在火，还有其他类似的工具，但 Eden 里的发现流也可以。

sentences.en: It's a tool. This is what writers use.
sentences.zh: 它是一个工具。这就是写作者用的东西。

sentences.en: They use it research tools to actually research the market if they don't want to do it manually.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不想手动做市场调研，就会用这类研究工具来真正研究市场。

sentences.en: But of course you can do it manually.
sentences.zh: 但你当然也可以手动来做。

sentences.en: And one of my favorite things to do is to look for a specific creator and then go to their actual account and then filter their content by top light.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢做的一件事，就是找一个特定的创作者，然后去他的主页，按热度最高来筛选他的内容。

sentences.en: This is especially good if you're trying to get on YouTube and find YouTube titles, or just angles that people are already paying attention to, and then you can see people's top YouTube videos, or top posts, or top notes, or top articles, or top tweets, or top Instagram Reels or carousels or whatever it may be.
sentences.zh: 如果你想上 YouTube、找 YouTube 标题，或者找人们已经在关注的切入角度，这招特别好用，你可以看到别人最火的 YouTube 视频、最火的帖子、最火的笔记、最火的文章、最火的推文、最火的 Instagram Reels 或轮播图，什么都可以。

sentences.en: Then if you want to learn how to actually recreate it, just hit the reverse engineer button and then say, hey, I want to recreate this with my own idea, and then you're good to go.
sentences.zh: 然后如果你想学会怎么复刻它，就点一下逆向工程按钮，告诉它：嘿，我想用自己的想法复刻这个，然后你就可以开始了。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what I did for this video and the newsletter that I wrote previously for this, the the topic that inspired this video was a video that got like 700,000 views, and it was called the Notebook System that saved my brain.
sentences.zh: 我这期视频就是这么做的，我之前为这个主题写的 newsletter 也是这么来的——启发这期视频的那个视频大概有 70 万播放，标题叫《拯救了我大脑的笔记本系统》。

sentences.en: I looked at that and I'm like, What about the writing system that saved my brain?
sentences.zh: 我看到那个标题就想：那拯救了我大脑的写作系统呢？

sentences.en: What about the writing habit that saved my brain?
sentences.zh: 拯救了我大脑的写作习惯呢？

sentences.en: And the title may not reflect that right now, but it was a good starting point for the idea that I could then write about.
sentences.zh: 现在的标题可能还没体现出这一点，但它是一个很好的起点，让我可以围绕这个想法去写。

sentences.en: And of course, I can craft the the title and thumbnail later on.
sentences.zh: 当然，标题和封面我可以之后再打磨。

sentences.en: If I come up with a better idea.
sentences.zh: 如果我想到更好的想法的话。

sentences.en: That may or may not work because none of this is guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 这可能会奏效，也可能不会，因为这一切都没有保证。

sentences.en: So once you have something to write about, what I personally do is create one project for the entire week because I post one newsletter to Substack, which is also an article on Substack.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你有了可以写的东西，我个人的做法是为一整周创建一个项目，因为我每周在 Substack 上发一篇 newsletter，它同时也是 Substack 上的一篇文章。

sentences.en: I copy paste that to X articles, which gets posted there as well, copy pasted, that eventually turns into a soft YouTube script, and then the YouTube video gets uploaded to podcast channels, and then I can use the original newsletter for tweet ideas throughout the week, or as ideas just come to mind,
sentences.zh: 我把它复制粘贴到 X 文章上，也在那里发布，再复制粘贴，最终变成一个软性的 YouTube 脚本，然后 YouTube 视频会被上传到播客频道，接着我可以用最初的 newsletter 来构思一周里的推文创意，或者当想法自然冒出来的时候，

sentences.en: I can write the tweets as well.
sentences.zh: 我也可以直接写推文。

sentences.en: And then those get cross posted to Substack notes, and then I turn them into images that I can post on Instagram and LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 然后这些推文会被交叉发布到 Substack 笔记上，我再把它们转成图片，发到 Instagram 和 LinkedIn。

sentences.en: And then for some of the tweets that I really like, I'll just sit in front of the camera and read the tweet to the camera and boom!
sentences.zh: 然后对于那些我特别喜欢的推文，我就直接坐在镜头前，对着镜头把那条推文读出来，砰！

sentences.en: Now I have reels, TikToks and shorts, and it only took an hour or two every day.
sentences.zh: 现在我就有了 Reels、TikToks 和 Shorts，每天只花一两个小时。

sentences.en: And frankly, any more content than that, I know there's Alex Hermosa and other people who just want you to push more, more and more and more volume.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，再多做任何内容——我知道有 Alex Hermosa 和其他人，他们只想让你堆量、堆更多、更多、更多的量。

sentences.en: But everyone's doing that, right.
sentences.zh: 但所有人都在这么做，对吧。

sentences.en: If you want a competitive advantage, do something different.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要一个竞争优势，就做点不一样的事。

sentences.en: Tone it down, increase the quality of the things that you're doing, and make them impossible to ignore.
sentences.zh: 把节奏放慢，把你做的事情的质量提上去，让它们变得无法被忽视。

sentences.en: Add a bit of scarcity to your brand so people are not just overloaded with it, they have to wait for you to actually post something.
sentences.zh: 给你的品牌加一点稀缺感，这样人们不会信息过载，他们得等你真正发东西。

sentences.en: And when they do see something from you, they aren't used to it.
sentences.zh: 当他们真的看到你发的内容时，他们不会觉得习以为常。

sentences.en: It's a dopamine hit for them when that's not happening for any other creator that they look at.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说是一次多巴胺冲击，而他们关注的其他创作者已经给不了这种感觉了。

sentences.en: So when I have the topic that I want to write about, I create a project around it.
sentences.zh: 所以当我有了想写的主题，我会围绕它创建一个项目。

sentences.en: I create a board. Of course, this can be a notion page.
sentences.zh: 我创建一个看板。当然，这也可以是一个 Notion 页面。

sentences.en: You can write wherever you want.
sentences.zh: 你在哪里写都可以。

sentences.en: But now what I do once I have the topic is all create an outline note and then inside of here, I'll just write out certain things that I think should be in here.
sentences.zh: 但现在我有了主题之后，会先创建一个大纲笔记，然后在里面写下一些我认为应该包含的内容。

sentences.en: This is an even close to fleshed out.
sentences.zh: 这离真正充实起来还差得远。

sentences.en: It's just the ideas that came to mind so that I could start to create some kind of structure.
sentences.zh: 只是那些冒出来的想法，这样我可以开始搭建某种结构。

sentences.en: Then inside of the board itself, I paste links to YouTube videos inside of here that I think would have good ideas that I could use inside of the newsletter, and then I can have a chats open alongside me as I write and just ask questions when I need them, or I can reference videos from inside of the board.
sentences.zh: 然后在看板里，我会粘贴一些 YouTube 视频链接，我觉得这些视频里有好的想法可以用到 newsletter 里，接着我写作时可以在旁边开着聊天窗口，需要的时候随时提问，或者我也可以直接参考看板里的视频。

sentences.en: If I create a new chat, click on this video and then I just ask it for questions to pull the ideas that I need from inside of it, and then I can quit capture ideas into this board as well, so that I can just have them with me as I'm writing, which is honestly a dream come true for any writer, you know how valuable this can be.
sentences.zh: 如果我新建一个聊天，点击这个视频，然后直接让它提问，帮我提取里面需要的想法，我也可以把想法捕捉到这个看板里，这样写作时它们就在手边，说实话这对任何写作者来说都是梦想成真，你知道这有多宝贵。

sentences.en: And then when it comes to generating title ideas or things like that, I just referenced the newsletter in the chat and then if I want them to be data backed,
sentences.zh: 然后到了生成标题创意之类的时候，我就在聊天里引用那期 newsletter，如果我想让标题有数据支撑，

sentences.en: I can have it search for a specific creator's titles, or I can reference swipe files inside of my board because I've saved ideas before.
sentences.zh: 我可以让它搜索某个特定创作者的标题，或者参考我看板里的 swipe files，因为我之前已经保存过想法了。

sentences.en: So I have an entire database of YouTube videos and titles that I think work really well inside of here, so I can look through these when it's time to generate ideas for how I want to actually package the newsletter YouTube video that I'm putting out.
sentences.zh: 所以我在这里面有一整个 YouTube 视频和标题的数据库，都是我认为效果很好的，当我需要为即将发布的 newsletter 或 YouTube 视频构思包装方式时，就可以翻看这些。

sentences.en: So, so far, the entire process is just capture ideas as they come to mind and save inspiration.
sentences.zh: 所以，到目前为止，整个流程就是：想法冒出来就捕捉，灵感来了就保存。

sentences.en: Save the posts that you like that did really well, that have good title structures, that have good ideas in general.
sentences.zh: 保存你喜欢的、表现很好的帖子，那些标题结构好、整体想法好的帖子。

sentences.en: Jot down your own ideas and then you create one topic per week and just have that as a project, a central project where you can put all of your research.
sentences.zh: 快速记下你自己的想法，然后每周创建一个主题，把它当作一个项目，一个中心项目，所有研究都可以放进去。

sentences.en: You can create a note, you can add a bunch of links in there if you want, or you can create a board and just paste everything in, and then you can write with your research alongside it.
sentences.zh: 你可以创建一个笔记，想加链接就加一堆进去，或者创建一个看板把所有东西都粘贴进去，然后你就可以在研究材料就在旁边的情况下写作。

sentences.en: And then all you really do is you just outline, right and repurpose as we kind of sort of discussed, but outlining and learning how to structure newsletters, that's like the topic for an entirely new video.
sentences.zh: 然后你真正要做的，就是写大纲、写作和内容复用，我们之前大概聊过，但写大纲和学会如何构建 newsletter，那完全是另一个视频的主题了。

sentences.en: So instead, what I found in the discord, someone created a guide for my top Substack articles for how they're structured.
sentences.zh: 所以反过来，我在 Discord 里发现，有人做了一个指南，分析了我最受欢迎的 Substack 文章是怎么结构的。

sentences.en: And what I did is I took those and I turned it into a prompt that will ask you for what you want to talk about and then help guide you to creating your first newsletter.
sentences.zh: 我做的就是把这些拿过来，转化成一个提示词，它会问你你想聊什么，然后引导你创作你的第一期 newsletter。

sentences.en: So if you actually want to use that prompt, there's a link to it in the description, and that alone will help you write your first newsletter if you want to, or your first article, or your first YouTube script or whatever it may be.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你真的想用那个提示词，描述区里有链接，光靠这个就能帮你写出你的第一期 newsletter，如果你想的话，或者第一篇文、第一个 YouTube 脚本，什么都行。

sentences.en: So that's the entire system.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个系统。

sentences.en: Walking, reading, and about 60 minutes a day of writing forms the foundation for some of the most future proof skills learning, thinking, and earning independently.
sentences.zh: 散步、阅读，加上每天大约 60 分钟的写作，构成了最面向未来的技能基础：学习、思考、独立赚钱。

sentences.en: So I'll leave it at that.
sentences.zh: 我就说到这里。

sentences.en: I'm happy to expand on it more in the future, but if you want to watch more on it now, it actually highly recommend watching my last video, which goes over how to pull psychological levers to get people to pay more attention, and that complements writing very nicely.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意以后展开讲更多，但如果你想现在就多看一些，我强烈推荐看我上一期视频，讲的是如何拉动心理杠杆让人们投入更多注意力，这和写作搭配起来非常好。

sentences.en: Thank you for watching.
sentences.zh: 感谢观看。

sentences.en: Links to the boot camp and prompt in the description.
sentences.zh: 训练营和提示词的链接在描述区。

sentences.en: I'll see you in the next video. Bye!
sentences.zh: 下期视频见。拜！
